title: Charlie Cordella and other overlooked clarinetists
summary: Cordella was an excellent but unrecognised clarinetist; he tries to recall another Italian player at Pete Herman's.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Charlie Cordillo?
Yeah, not too much because he played the same instrument. I mean in those, like in smaller bands they were very seldom usable, one clarinet or sax. But Charlie played excellent clarinet.
Well that's a man that's played with good bands and has never gotten much recognition. That's funny you know.

Charlie Cordella and another one is, well let me think, he and Charlie worked together quite a while. Years ago there was a band at Pete Hermans before I ever went there. Sharky had the band I believe. Chink Martin played in it and Freddie Newman and Charlie Cordella and Sidney Ayrton played together. And then another boy, Ray, he played very well and he never did get any recognition either.
He played clarinet and sax. Ray, uh. Not Ray Burke?
Harry Raymond? No, this was Italian boy. You know I know his name, I can't think of it. I'll come to you in a minute.
